newsitem.title: JAPAN: Key JGBs up on Fed, then shed gains on hedge sales.
newsitem.headline: Key JGBs up on Fed, then shed gains on hedge sales.

text.p: Key December Japanese government bond futures rose on Wednesday, following the Fed's decision overnight to leave interest rates unchanged, but gains were pared on hedge sales after a JGB auction.

The December contract opened sharply higher at 122.40, in the wake of the Federal Open Market Committee (FOMC) meeting, which opted to keep interest rates steady, contrary to many market players' expectations.
"Day-traders often go long at the open on such a day," said a trader at a city bank. But as soon as they found the contract was unlikely to rise further, they started to dump them."
After the market finished digesting the U.S. cantral bank's lack of action, it started to look at a factor of it own -- an auction of 10-year JGBs.

The Ministry of Finance (MOF) announced this morning that the coupon rate on the JGBs to be offered was set at 2.9 percent. The decision also cheered the market, as a lower coupon rate could have deterred many investors, dealers said.

The market made another try for the top in the afternoon, relying on talk that the auction would produce better results than expected. There were rumours that some city banks had placed bids in the auction, dealers said.
But hedge sales linked to the auction blocked the contract again and pushed it back to near the day's low.
One trader at a long-term credit bank said weak data announced on Wednesday -- August domestic vehicle production and August large chain store sales -- also contributed in bringing down the contract.
Car production fell by 2.1 percent and chain store sales dropped by 0.2 percent, both year-on-year.
The December contract closed near its day's low, at 122.28, which was still 0.17 higher than Tuesday. Volume was 62,818 contracts.
A dealer at a securities firm said the market would be heading in the direction of filling the gap between today's low of 122.25 and Tuesday's high of 122.17 in the next few days.
But dealers also said today's auction revealed that investors' demand for JGBs continues to underpin the market.
Many dealers said cash bonds took the lead in the market today. The benchmark 182nd 10-year JGBs were yielding 2.800 percent, down 0.045 from Tuesday, as of 0729 GMT.
The yield hit 2.790 percent at one point, its low for this year. Dealers said the benchmark cash JGBs also became the target of hedge sales.

In the morning session, the 170th and 174th JGBs were heavily bought, some dealers said. These bonds looked cheaper after longer yields were bought, said a dealer at a securities firm. -- Hideyuki Sano, Tokyo Treasury Desk (81-3-3432-8586)
